newsitem.title: UK: SBS-AGRO to set first Eurobond for a Russian bank.
newsitem.headline: SBS-AGRO to set first Eurobond for a Russian bank.

text.p: SBS-AGRO said on Wednesday it would launch the first mainstream Eurobond for a Russian bank next week.
The deal, to be lead managed by JP Morgan, is expected to have a three-year maturity with a size around $150 million.
Representatives from SBS-AGRO, one of Russia's largest private banks, were in London to meet investors ahead of the bond's launch.
"Extending the bank's funding maturity remains a priority in 1997," SBS-AGRO's head of international business development Alexander Lossik said.
SBS-AGRO -- rated B1 by Moody's, B+ by S&P and BB by IBCA -- has the largest branch network of any private bank with 1,400 branches located throughout Russia, Lossik said.
Russia opened the sluice gates for the region last November with the launch of its first Eurobond, a $1.0 billion five-year offering. It has since launched two more bonds, in marks and dollars.
The Russian cities of Moscow and St Petersburg have also tapped the market, but so far the long list of banks and corporates waiting to raise funds abroad have not come to market.
Lossik said SBS-AGRO would establish an ECP (Euro Commercial Paper) programme later this year.
In 1989 Bank Stolichny was established as a co-operative bank to serve construction clients. In 1992 traditional banking extended to include capital markets, privatisation and advisory services.

In 1994 it was licensed to deal in gold, precious metals and foreign securities and changed its name to Stolichny Bank of Savings (SBS). In 1996 SBS won the Agroprombank tender and acquired control changing its name to SBS-AGRO. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
